security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan's Load-Store Queue (LSQ), when store-to-load forwarding searches matching stores for a load after MDB, if the age-based CAM/tag match logic incorrectly forwards from a non-youngest matching store (e.g., due to CAM returning first hit instead of youngest hit, or due to a partial address match on a store that is not the last one in program order), the load obtains data from a store older than the 'last' store to the same physical address, violating the tightened MDB semantics that require forwarding from precisely the last preceding store.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: store-to-load forwarding CAM search that does not prioritize youngest/last matching store by program order; LSQ age comparison using stale/incomplete store-mask bits; load-forwarding path that selects first CAM match instead of walking all matches to find the most recent
security_spec.summary: Tightened MDB spec from 'an instruction that stores' to 'the last instruction that stores' — LSQ forwarding must guarantee youngest-match selection; any bug selecting a non-last matching store lets post-MDB loads observe stale data, breaking the barrier and enabling Spectre-style data leaks past the speculation fence.
